turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
From the training set, the strongest candidates are the ones that closely reproduce the highest-efficiency design rules while adding only modest, physically beneficial modifications:

1. **c038** is essentially the 20.0%-efficient FTO / PCBM-60 / Au-np:NiO-c / Ag architecture, with a thin PEI interlayer. PEI can improve interface dipole/passivation without destroying the excellent electron extraction of PCBM and the high-work-function Au-np:NiO-c contact. This is the most direct descendant of a proven high-efficiency stack.

2. **c030** closely matches the 19.48% ITO / PCBM-60:Bphen / PTAA:PMMA / Al family. PTAA:PMMA is associated with high-quality, hydrophobic perovskite films and reduced interfacial recombination, while Bphen/IDTT2FPDI can provide a better electron-selective cascade.

3. **c044** is a close analog of the 18.6–18.9% PCBM/C60:BCP / PTAA / Cu devices. PTAA/Cu gives good hole selectivity and ohmic collection, while BCP provides hole blocking and interface passivation.

4. **c041** combines the successful FTO/PCBM/BCP electron-side concept with NiMgLiO-c, a high-work-function, selective NiO-based HTL seen in the 18%+ training region. It should have strong band alignment and good selectivity.

5. **c097** is the selenium-substituted analog of the 18.49% ITCPTC-Th/C60:BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag family, and P3CT-Na-containing devices repeatedly appear in the high-efficiency part of the training data. The C60:BCP electron-selective stack plus P3CT-Na hole extraction is physically very sound.

Final: c038, c030, c044, c041, c097
